the most effective and efficient production management information system (PMIS) is a hybrid system that is a mix of both a transaction processing system (TPS) and a management information system (MIS).
the production manager's task can be divided into three task areas: capacity establishment, capacity utilisation, and production control.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a comprehensive model for the production management system that is capable of providing a framework for the design, implementation, and evaluation of production management systems.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the task assignment approach is a more complete and realistic description of the production management function than the information‐based approach.
the production management system must provide for a variety of information needs, and must be able to adapt to changes in the organisation.
the task assignment‐task structuring approach is a more realistic and useful approach than the traditional information systems approach to the development of production management systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
production management needs a more comprehensive approach to information systems.
production management systems should be designed to match task structuring and task assignment to the needs and capabilities of management and workers.
we are trying to understand the role of technology in the production management system and to understand how technology can help production management.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the production management system is a complex, multifaceted system that is not well served by the current literature.
the production management system is a dynamic and evolving system.
production managers are not just interested in the technology of information systems, but also in the human resources that are available for production tasks.
